blueprint.name: English
blueprint.source: CDS Paper I English: 120 questions, 100 marks, 2 hours; negative 1/3.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelled word that describes something temporary and short-lived.
questions.solution: 'Ephemeral' is the correct spelling, derived from Greek meaning 'lasting for a day'. The other options contain letter transpositions ('Epemeral', 'Efemeral') or substitution errors ('Ephemrel').

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: 'He is allergic _____ peanuts.'
questions.solution: The standard collocation for allergies is 'allergic to'. We say someone is allergic to a specific substance. Other prepositions like 'with', 'on', or 'at' are grammatically incorrect in this context.

questions.text: Arrange the jumbled sentences into a coherent paragraph: P: It has a population of over 20 million. Q: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. R: The city is famous for its modern skyline. S: Visitors come from all over the world to see it.
questions.solution: The logical flow starts with introducing the subject: 'Tokyo is the capital of Japan' (Q). Next, a specific detail about the city follows: 'It has a population...' (P), where 'It' refers to Tokyo. Then, another description: 'The city is famous...' (R). Finally, a concluding statement about visitors: 'Visitors come...' (S). Thus, Q-P-S-R creates a smooth narrative.

questions.text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'Benevolent':
questions.solution: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly. Its direct antonym is 'Malevolent', which implies wishing harm or evil upon others. 'Kind', 'Generous', and 'Compassionate' are synonyms or related positive traits.

questions.text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'Candid'.
questions.solution: 'Candid' means truthful, straightforward, or frank. 'Frank', 'Honest', and 'Direct' are synonyms. 'Reserved' implies holding back feelings or being quiet, which is the opposite of being open and candid.

questions.text: Identify the error in the following sentence: 'The committee have decided to postpone the meeting.'
questions.solution: The word 'committee' refers to a group of people and is treated as a plural noun. Therefore, it requires the plural verb 'have', not the singular 'has'. The sentence structure and other verbs are grammatically correct.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: 'She is very fond _____ classical music.'
questions.solution: The phrase 'fond of' is a fixed idiomatic expression used to indicate liking or affection for something. The prepositions 'to', 'on', and 'at' do not collocate with the adjective 'fond'.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelled word that means 'a large number of people'.
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'Multitude', referring to a great number. The other options contain transposition or omission errors: 'Mulltitude' has double 'l' in the wrong place, 'Mutltitude' swaps 'l' and 't', and 'Multitute' omits an 'i'.

questions.text: One-word substitution: A person who is afraid of heights is called a _______.
questions.solution: 'Acrophobia' is the fear of heights; thus, a person suffering from it is an 'Acrophobe'. 'Hydrophobe' fears water, 'Arachnophobic' (often spelled Arachnophobe) fears spiders, and 'Claustrophobic' fears enclosed spaces.

options.label: A
options.text: A universal cure for all diseases

questions.solution: 'Panacea' comes from Greek and literally means 'a cure-all'. It is used metaphorically to describe a solution or remedy that is believed to be effective for every problem. The other options describe completely different concepts unrelated to the definition.

questions.text: Which option correctly completes the sentence: 'Neither the teacher nor the students _____ aware of the schedule change.'?
questions.solution: When a subject is connected by 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the noun closest to it. Here, 'students' (plural) is closer to the blank than 'teacher'. Therefore, the plural verb 'are' is required.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelled word that means 'a person who is skilled in many arts or sciences'.
questions.solution: 'Polymath' is the correct spelling for a person of wide-ranging knowledge. The other options are misspelled variations with incorrect letter arrangements or missing letters.

questions.text: Arrange the jumbled sentences into a coherent paragraph: P: It is known as the Gateway to India. Q: The monument was built in 1862. R: Located at Nariman Point in Mumbai. S: This structure features a large archway.
questions.solution: The logical flow begins with location (R), followed by the description of the structure and its famous name (P), then historical details (Q), and finally specific architectural features (S). This order creates a natural introduction to the landmark before providing details.

questions.text: What does the idiom 'Beat around the bush' mean?

options.label: A
options.text: A) To avoid the main issue directly

options.label: B
options.text: B) To prepare a garden for planting

options.label: C
options.text: C) To walk quickly to reach a destination

questions.solution: This idiom means to avoid speaking about or dealing with the main point of something, usually because one is shy, nervous, or trying to evade a difficult topic. The other options describe literal actions or unrelated behaviors.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled word that describes a person who speaks their mind frankly:
questions.solution: The correct spelling is 'Candid', derived from the Latin 'candere' meaning to shine or be frank. The options 'Candid', 'Candid', and 'Canide' contain incorrect letter arrangements that do not form valid English words in this context.
